adventure.title: Fly the SlotZilla Zipline Down Fremont
adventure.description: Launch from a twelve-story slot machine and fly superhero-style under the Fremont Street canopy while a million LEDs strobe overhead and the crowd hollers below.
adventure.bonus: Take the upper Zoomline, arms out, eyes open the whole way.

adventure.title: Get Lost in Omega Mart at AREA15
adventure.description: Meow Wolf's supermarket-gone-wrong starts as a grocery store and unravels into a portal-riddled art dimension — pull every handle, read every label, trust no product.
adventure.bonus: Find at least one hidden passage without watching anyone else use it first.

adventure.title: Expedition to Little Finland, Gold Butte
adventure.description: Deep in Gold Butte National Monument, wind-carved sandstone fins twist into alien architecture that appears on zero tourist maps — high-clearance vehicle required, solitude guaranteed.
adventure.bonus: Find a fin formation narrow enough to chimney up using just your back and legs, and get at least five feet off the ground.

adventure.title: Tandem Skydive Over the Las Vegas Strip
adventure.description: Jump from 15,000 feet with Skydive Las Vegas over Boulder City — sixty seconds of freefall with Lake Mead below you and the Strip shimmering on the horizon.
adventure.bonus: During freefall, spread your arms completely, close your eyes, and count to ten before opening them again.

adventure.title: Cross the Hoover Dam Arch Bridge on Foot
adventure.description: Walk the Mike O'Callaghan–Pat Tillman Memorial Bridge 900 feet above the Colorado River for a vertiginous look straight down at the dam's concrete crown.
adventure.bonus: Stop at the midpoint, lean over the railing as far as you dare, and hold a still photo looking straight down — no guardrail cropping allowed.

adventure.title: Sunrise at Valley of Fire State Park
adventure.description: Drive 55 miles northeast of the Strip to watch Nevada's oldest state park ignite in orange and crimson at first light — ancient petroglyphs included.
adventure.bonus: Hike to Atlatl Rock, climb the metal staircase, and press your palm flat against a petroglyph panel — quietly, respectfully.

adventure.title: Shoot Full-Auto at Machine Guns Vegas
adventure.description: Unload a Tommy gun, an AK-47, and an M249 SAW at a professional indoor range staffed by ex-military instructors who take zero nonsense.
adventure.bonus: Ask to fire the .50-caliber Barrett and keep your grouping inside a dinner-plate-sized circle at 50 yards.

adventure.title: Indoor Skydive at iFLY Las Vegas
adventure.description: Step into the vertical wind tunnel off the Strip and learn to hover, flip, and carve through air at 120 mph without the 15,000-foot drop.
adventure.bonus: Get the instructor to take you to the top of the tunnel on your second flight — the ceiling is where it gets real.

adventure.title: Drive a Race Car with Dream Racing at LVMS
adventure.description: Dream Racing straps you into a real race car at Las Vegas Motor Speedway and lets you push it on actual banked track — the Strip's roller coasters are embarrassed.
adventure.bonus: Ask the instructor to let you take Turn 1 without lifting the throttle — then actually do it.

adventure.title: Walk the Neon Museum Boneyard at Night
adventure.description: Wander through Las Vegas's graveyard of retired casino signs after dark, where the city's entire gaudy history rusts beautifully under a desert sky.
adventure.bonus: Find the original Stardust sign and take a portrait photo using only the ambient neon for light — no flash allowed.

adventure.title: Float the Colorado at Emerald Cave
adventure.description: Kayak through Black Canyon on the Colorado River until you reach a glowing green grotto that looks like a screensaver made real.
adventure.bonus: Swim into the cave and touch the back wall — cold water and all.

adventure.title: Hike the Calico Hills at Red Rock Canyon
adventure.description: Scramble up rust-red sandstone formations at dawn before the desert heat and tour buses arrive, with nothing but jackrabbits and silence for company.
adventure.bonus: Free-solo a boulder face at least 10 feet off the ground and hold the summit pose for a full minute.

foodie.title: 3 A.M. at the Peppermill Fireside Lounge
foodie.description: Since 1972, the Peppermill's neon-lit dining room and sunken fire pit lounge have fed and sheltered every kind of Vegas night — order a scorpion bowl and a plate of fruit the size of a hubcap.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the fire pit, not the dining room — and stay past the point that feels reasonable.

foodie.title: Ramen at Monta Japanese Noodle House
foodie.description: Chinatown's most consistent ramen counter draws a loyal Japanese expat crowd for tonkotsu that takes no shortcuts.
foodie.bonus: Slurp loudly — it's correct here — and add the extra chashu without second-guessing yourself.

foodie.title: Steakhouse Lunch at Ellis Island Casino
foodie.description: This off-Strip locals' casino has served its famously cheap off-menu steak special for decades — an honest slab of sirloin, a beer from the in-house brewery, and zero irony.
foodie.bonus: Play $5 on a video poker machine at the bar before your steak arrives and let it ride.

foodie.title: Craft Cocktails at Herbs & Rye
foodie.description: One of Vegas's original serious cocktail bars pours pre-Prohibition classics with obsessive precision until 3 a.m. every night.
foodie.bonus: Tell the bartender your mood in three words and order whatever they build — no veto.

foodie.title: Sandwich at the Bagelmania Deli
foodie.description: A no-frills Vegas institution since 1984, Bagelmania feeds locals oversized deli sandwiches before the tourists are even awake.
foodie.bonus: Order a lox bagel with extra capers and eat it at the counter reading whatever newspaper is lying around.

foodie.title: Dim Sum at Ping Pang Pong at Gold Coast
foodie.description: Locals bypass the Strip entirely for this Gold Coast institution where carts roll non-stop and the har gow is flawless.
foodie.bonus: Point at something from the cart you can't identify and eat it without asking what it is.

foodie.title: Omakase at Kabuto Edomae Sushi
foodie.description: This quiet ten-seat room in Chinatown delivers one of the most precise and intimate Edomae omakase experiences in the American West — phones down, fish up.
foodie.bonus: Let the chef choose your sake pairing without asking the price — commit fully.

foodie.title: Pasta Night at Esther's Kitchen
foodie.description: The Arts District's defining restaurant packs a devoted crowd for handmade pasta, sourdough with cultured butter, and a wine list worth crossing town for — book ahead or eat at the bar.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the counter and strike up a conversation with whoever's next to you — odds are they're a local chef.

foodie.title: Lunch at Lotus of Siam
foodie.description: The most respected Thai restaurant in America serves incendiary northern Thai dishes that regulars chase from across the country.
foodie.bonus: Order the nam kao tod and ask your server to bring it Thai-spicy — no modifications.

foodie.title: Find Secret Pizza at the Cosmopolitan
foodie.description: Navigate the unmarked third-floor corridor at the Cosmopolitan — no signage, no reservations — and eat a genuinely great New York slice surrounded by people who found it the same way you did.
foodie.bonus: Find the place without using Google Maps — use only the Cosmopolitan's elevator bank and word of mouth from one stranger.

foodie.title: Late-Night Tacos at Tacos El Gordo on the Strip
foodie.description: Join the 2 a.m. line of cooks, dealers, and savvy tourists at this Tijuana-style taqueria and eat adobada carved straight off a trompo until the city finally makes sense.
foodie.bonus: Order the cabeza taco and eat it entirely before looking up what it is.

foodie.title: Dinner at Joël Robuchon at MGM Grand
foodie.description: Settle into the most Michelin-starred restaurant in Las Vegas history for a sixteen-course tasting menu inside a Belle Époque dining room that treats dinner like theater.
foodie.bonus: Order the legendary pomme purée as a standalone course and ask your server the exact butter-to-potato ratio — then order a second portion.

active.title: Hike Mary Jane Falls at Mount Charleston
active.description: Forty-five minutes from the Strip, the switchbacks up Kyle Canyon end at a spring-fed waterfall and cave alcoves 25 degrees cooler than the valley floor — the desert's escape hatch.
active.bonus: Stand in the spray at the falls — then dry off on the descent with the whole valley below you.

active.title: Public Skate at City National Arena
active.description: Skate the Golden Knights' practice facility in Summerlin during public sessions — NHL ice, cheap rentals, and a nonzero chance the team is drilling on the other sheet.
active.bonus: One full lap skating backwards — desert kids get no excuses.

active.title: Run the Wetlands Park Nature Preserve Trails
active.description: Clark County's 290-acre Wetlands Park is a flat, bird-rich trail system on the city's eastern edge that feels nothing like Las Vegas and is completely free.
active.bonus: Spot and photograph at least five different bird species before you loop back to the trailhead.

active.title: Golf the Bali Hai Golf Club at Sunrise
active.description: The only golf course on the Strip proper — a lush tropical layout that looks absurd against the desert skyline — and it plays best before the heat takes over.
active.bonus: Bet a round of drinks on the back nine with whoever you're playing — pay up immediately at the 19th hole.

active.title: Pick Up a Game at Sunset Park Basketball Courts
active.description: The full-court outdoor games at Sunset Park run seven days a week and draw a serious level of local talent that will test your game fast.
active.bonus: Call your own five-person squad and challenge the court winners — losers sit out a full game.

active.title: Swim at Lake Mead's Boulder Beach
active.description: Nevada's only real beach is a legitimately beautiful stretch of warm desert water where locals actually swim, paddleboard, and forget the Strip exists.
active.bonus: Swim out to the buoy line and back without touching the bottom — then lie flat on the sand until you've caught your breath.

active.title: Morning Ride on the River Mountains Loop Trail
active.description: This 34-mile paved loop through Boulder City and Henderson serves up volcanic ridgelines, Lake Mead views, and zero traffic — a road cyclist's secret.
active.bonus: Complete the full loop without stopping except to refill water — no café breaks, no bail-outs.

active.title: Rock Climb at Red Rock Climbing Center
active.description: The largest indoor climbing gym in Nevada gives you a serious burn and a community of locals who treat this desert sport like a religion.
active.bonus: Attempt a route one grade above your comfort level and don't come down until you've made it past the crux.

active.title: Lap the Las Vegas Strip on Foot at Midnight
active.description: Walking the full Strip from Mandalay Bay to the Stratosphere after dark hits different — the neon, the chaos, and the crowd are the whole point.
active.bonus: Stop at every free spectacle — Bellagio fountains, the Mirage volcano, and the Venetian canals — without setting foot inside a casino.

active.title: Tennis at Darling Tennis Center
active.description: The best public tennis facility in the desert has 22 lighted courts and a walk-up culture where locals challenge strangers to sets without ceremony.
active.bonus: Walk up and challenge the best player warming up on court 1 — tell them you're new in town.

active.title: Mountain Bike the Bootleg Canyon Trails in Boulder City
active.description: Just 30 minutes from the Strip, Bootleg Canyon's network of purpose-built singletrack descends 1,000 feet through the Mojave with zero tourists in sight.
active.bonus: Clean the Deuces Wild descent without putting a foot down — if you fail, ride it again.

active.title: Sunrise Run Along the Las Vegas Wash Trail
active.description: Hit the paved multiuse path along the Las Vegas Wash at first light for a flat, fast, five-mile route through open desert wetlands that feels nothing like the city surrounding it.
active.bonus: Run the full five miles without earbuds — just the sound of the wash, the birds, and your own breathing.

social.title: Late Round at the Double Down Saloon
social.description: The punk-rock dive that never closes and never had a cover — house rules on the wall, bacon martinis on request, and a jukebox with genuine taste.
social.bonus: Order the Ass Juice. Ask zero questions first.

social.title: Karaoke with Danny G at Dino's Lounge
social.description: Las Vegas's self-proclaimed 'last neighborhood bar' has held down the same Strip-adjacent corner since 1962 — the weekend karaoke is legendary, merciless, and completely welcoming.
social.bonus: Sing something. Not maybe. The room respects attempts, not perfection.

social.title: Sunday Brunch at Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan
social.description: One of the best buffets in Vegas history — individually plated stations, serious ingredient quality, and bottomless mimosas that make it a full social event.
social.bonus: Plate a full round from every single station before going back for seconds on anything.

social.title: Blackjack Session at El Cortez Hotel & Casino
social.description: The oldest continuously operating hotel-casino in Las Vegas still has single-deck blackjack, $5 minimums, and a perfectly preserved mid-century Fremont Street vibe.
social.bonus: Set a strict $50 buy-in limit and walk the moment you double it — no exceptions, no 'just one more hand.'

social.title: Afternoon at the Pinball Hall of Fame
social.description: Over 200 vintage pinball machines from the 1950s to today, all playable — this nonprofit hall at the south end of the Strip is one of the most authentically weird rooms in the city.
social.bonus: Find the oldest working machine in the room and post a high score before moving to any modern one.

social.title: Speakeasy Cocktails at The Laundry Room
social.description: You text a secret number, get a reservation, and descend into a 10-seat cocktail bar inside a broom closet at Commonwealth — one of America's most clever hidden bars.
social.bonus: Tell the bartender your drink preferences but no spirit — let them build you something completely blind and drink all of it.

social.title: Watch an UNLV Runnin' Rebels Game at the Thomas & Mack Center
social.description: College basketball in a city without an NBA team hits with surprising intensity — the Thomas & Mack is loud, cheap, and genuinely fun.
social.bonus: Learn one Rebel's name before tip-off and root for only that player — loudly — the entire game.

social.title: Late Night at Commonwealth on Fremont East
social.description: Commonwealth's rooftop bar and ornate Victorian interior make it the sharpest cocktail destination on Fremont East, and it only gets better after midnight.
social.bonus: Move between all three levels — ground bar, mezzanine, rooftop — and order a different drink on each one.

social.title: Axe Throwing at Axe Monkeys Las Vegas
social.description: This no-frills axe-throwing lane spot in the northwest part of the city is where locals actually come to blow off steam — coached, competitive, and deeply satisfying.
social.bonus: Issue a sudden-death bullseye challenge to your group — whoever hits it last buys the first round.

social.title: Poolside at the Cosmopolitan's Boulevard Pool
social.description: The Cosmopolitan's Strip-facing pool deck is Vegas at its most absurdly cinematic — rent a daybed and let the city perform for you.
social.bonus: Introduce yourself to the group next to you and invite them to split a bottle — worst they can say is no.

social.title: Last Call at Frankie's Tiki Room
social.description: This 24-hour tiki temple on Charleston is exactly as unhinged as it sounds — potent house mugs, carved idols, and a crowd that has fully committed at every hour of the day.
social.bonus: Sing a song you don't know the words to — no phone allowed as a cheat sheet.

social.title: Bar Crawl on Fremont East Entertainment District
social.description: Work your way down Fremont East from The Griffin to Atomic Liquors — the oldest freestanding bar in Las Vegas — and experience the neighborhood bar scene locals built specifically to escape tourists.
social.bonus: Buy a round for a group of strangers, introduce yourself, and stay with them for at least one full hour.

chill.title: Soak in the Qua Baths & Spa at Caesars Palace
chill.description: Roman-themed thermal circuit pools, an arctic ice room, and an actual laconium — Caesars' day spa is excessive in the best possible way and genuinely restorative.
chill.bonus: Do the full thermal circuit in order — hot pool, steam room, ice room, laconium — without skipping the cold stage.

chill.title: Craft Cocktails at Velveteen Rabbit
chill.description: The Arts District's original cocktail bar mixes seasonal drinks and pours natural wine in a room that feels assembled from a beautifully curated dream — thrift-store chandeliers included.
chill.bonus: Sit at the outdoor patio, leave your phone in your bag, and write down three observations about the people who walk by.

chill.title: Sunset Drinks at the VooDoo Rooftop Lounge at Rio
chill.description: The 51st-floor open-air rooftop at the Rio delivers an unobstructed 360-degree Strip panorama at golden hour that almost no tourist knows about anymore.
chill.bonus: Get there 20 minutes before sunset, claim a rail spot, and don't touch your phone until the sun fully disappears.

chill.title: Morning Coffee at PublicUs
chill.description: The Arts District's best coffee-and-work room draws Vegas creatives, journalists, and regulars who treat it like a second living room.
chill.bonus: Leave your phone in your bag and spend 30 minutes doing nothing but watching the room.

chill.title: Watch a Show at The Smith Center for the Performing Arts
chill.description: Downtown's world-class performing arts venue books Broadway touring productions and jazz legends in a hall with acoustics that make any seat good.
chill.bonus: Go to the box office the day of and ask for whatever single seat is left — don't look it up in advance.

chill.title: Casino Hop the Old-School Locals' Casinos on Boulder Highway
chill.description: Boulder Station, Jokers Wild, and Arizona Charlie's Boulder form a stretch of unvarnished local gambling culture that Las Vegas pretends doesn't exist.
chill.bonus: Set a $20 limit at each stop — when it's gone, walk to the next one immediately.

chill.title: Sunset Picnic at Sunset Park
chill.description: Vegas locals have gathered at this 324-acre southeast-side park for decades — bring food, find the lake, and watch the light drain off the mountains.
chill.bonus: Challenge a stranger to a game of bocce or horseshoes at the courts — winner buys a drink nearby.

chill.title: Sit the Bellagio Conservatory & Botanical Garden
chill.description: The Bellagio's in-house horticulture team redesigns this massive conservatory five times a year with displays that are genuinely extraordinary.
chill.bonus: Stay long enough to watch at least two tour groups pass through while you sit completely still.

chill.title: Wander the Las Vegas Arts District on First Friday
chill.description: On the first Friday of every month, the 18b Arts District opens its galleries, food trucks, and studios to a crowd that's entirely not tourist.
chill.bonus: Buy a piece of original art from a local vendor — under $50, no prints.

chill.title: Read at the Clark County Library on Flamingo
chill.description: Slip off the Strip into one of the best-funded public library systems in Nevada, grab a window seat, and spend two hours pretending Las Vegas is a normal city.
chill.bonus: Strike up a genuine conversation with a local who's also reading and find out one thing about Las Vegas that doesn't appear in any guidebook.

chill.title: Afternoon at the Springs Preserve
chill.description: Spend a slow afternoon at the 180-acre desert oasis where Las Vegas's original artesian springs once flowed, with native botanical gardens and zero slot machines.
chill.bonus: Sit completely still on a bench in the butterfly garden for ten minutes and count how many species land within arm's reach.

chill.title: The Mob Museum, Then The Underground
chill.description: Three floors of organized-crime history inside the old federal courthouse, then descend to The Underground — the museum's working basement speakeasy and distillery — to debrief over a Prohibition-era cocktail.
chill.bonus: Spend two uninterrupted minutes alone in the courtroom where the 1950 Kefauver hearings were held with the lights off.
